item.title: Don't Believe Everything You Prove
item.description:
In many ways, this is a companion post to my complaint about John Backus’ Turing lecture. If you travel far enough along the smarter-than-thou asshole path, you’ll usually find the end of the line somewhere around formal proof methods.

The idea is that if we can elaborate a proof from a well-verified set of operations and a minimal collection of axioms, the thing we’re trying to demonstrate has to be correct. It’s the ultimate trump card for those seeking a pure, unassailable foundation for their program (or, increasingly, their philosophy of life).
